newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to raise tobacco tax, extend profit surtax.
newsitem.headline: Canada to raise tobacco tax, extend profit surtax.

text.p: Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin introduced in parliament on Thursday measures to raise tobacco taxes in four provinces and to extend a surtax on the profits of tobacco manufacturers.

The federal excise tax on cigarettes in Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick and Nova Scotia -- representing a majority of Canada's population -- is to be increased by C$0.70 (US$0.52) per carton of 200 cigarettes.
The three-year extension of the surtax on tobacco makers' profits, which continues at a rate of 40 percent, will raise C$65 million per fiscal year, the finance department said in a statement.

In addition, the four provinces will raise their cigarette taxes by C$0.70, yielding a total increase of C$1.40 per carton. The increase on cigarettes will raise an extra C$75 million per fiscal year for the federal government and will take effect at 2400 EDT Thursday/0500 GMT Friday.
Health Minister David Dingwall will later on Thursday unveil additional anti-tobacco measures, Martin said.

"The joint undertaking to increase federal and provincial tobacco tax rates follows the continued success of the anti-smuggling initiative and emphasizes the importance of federal-provincial efforts to deal effectively with contraband activity," Martin said in a statement. The federal government cut tobacco taxes in 1993 in an effort to counteract virulent cross-border cigarette smuggling from the United States.
